one_liner: Grows crops on land they own, rent or work - the occupation most Indians still live from.
job_roles: Farmer | Agricultural Labourer | Tenant Farmer & Sharecropper | Organic & Natural Farming Practitioner | Seed Grower | Contract Farming Cultivator | Farm Manager | Custom Hiring Operator | Farmer Producer Organisation Member
self_emp_route: Farming your own or leased land is self-employment by definition. What changes the income is not more land but a second engine: livestock, a Farmer Producer Organisation that aggregates and sells, custom hiring of machinery, or direct sale that skips the mandi.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed by AI, and that framing misses the point for this profession. The relevant technology is MECHANISATION and precision agriculture - drones, sensors, harvesters - which reduces the labour a hectare needs. That is good for a landowning farmer and bad for an Agricultural Labourer, who is the larger group. Advisory apps and image-based pest diagnosis substitute for extension advice rather than for the farmer.
role_spread: [Agricultural Labourer] higher: bodily, conscientiousness / lower: logical, openness || [Farm Manager, Contract Farming Cultivator] higher: logical, conscientiousness, reasoning, emotional_stability / lower: - || [Custom Hiring Operator] higher: logical, spatial, confidence / lower: agreeableness || [Organic & Natural Farming Practitioner] higher: naturalistic, openness, attention_span / lower: confidence
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None. This occupation is entered by inheritance far more often than by choice. -> land: Access to land - owned, inherited, leased or sharecropped. This, not a qualification, is the binding constraint. -> training: Krishi Vigyan Kendra training, state extension programmes, or a B.Sc Agriculture. None is required and most farmers have none. -> scale: Join a Farmer Producer Organisation, take up custom hiring, or add livestock - the documented routes to a viable income from a small holding.
review_reason: The verified figure is a HOUSEHOLD figure, not a personal income, and the schema has no way to say so - which risks a student reading 1.23 lakh as a salary. Two further gaps: no sourced figure for what a Farmer Producer Organisation membership or a custom hiring operation actually adds, which are the two documented routes upward, and no figure for agricultural labour daily wages, which is now the largest income source in farming households.
nuances: [economics] Verified, and it says something families are rarely told. An agricultural HOUSEHOLD earned Rs 10,218 a month in 2018-19 - about 1.23 lakh a year for a whole household - and only Rs 3,798 of it came from cultivation. Wages and salaries at Rs 4,063 are now the LARGER source. For most Indian farming families, farming is no longer the main source of the family's income. || [filter] Fails the compensation filter, and it is the largest occupation in the country. That is not an argument against the filter - the filter is telling the truth - but it is the sharpest illustration of why the application must be able to reverse it. A student from a farming family is not choosing whether farming pays; they are deciding what to do about a household that already lives on this. || [demand_signal] High is the right value and it needs care in reading. It means the work exists at enormous scale and is not disappearing, not that entering it is a good financial decision. Roughly 45 percent of Indian workers are in agriculture producing about 18 percent of GDP, which is the whole problem in one ratio.

one_liner: Works out how to grow more, better and with less - varieties, soil, pests, practice.
job_roles: Agronomist | Plant Breeder | Soil Scientist | Plant Pathologist | Entomologist | Seed Technologist | Agricultural Research Scientist | Crop Advisory Specialist | Precision Agriculture Specialist
entrance_exams: CUET (ICAR-UG) | State agricultural university admissions | ICAR ARS examination (Agricultural Research Service)
self_emp_route: Independent agronomy advisory, seed production on contract, or a consultancy to agritech and input companies. It depends on a reputation among farmers, which takes a decade.
ai_reason: Low exposure, protected by biology and by place. A model can read a research paper; it cannot run a multi-season varietal trial, judge a soil by handling it, or know why a recommendation that works in Punjab fails in Vidarbha. Crop Advisory Specialist carries the most exposure - image-based pest and disease diagnosis is genuinely good and is already deployed in farmer apps - but that displaces the routine half of advisory rather than the agronomist.
role_spread: [Plant Breeder, Agricultural Research Scientist] higher: reasoning, attention_span, long_term_memory / lower: extraversion || [Crop Advisory Specialist, Precision Agriculture Specialist] higher: verbal, logical, extraversion / lower: long_term_memory
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics, Chemistry and Biology; Agriculture as a subject where offered. Mathematics is accepted in place of Biology for some programmes. -> entrance_exam: State agricultural university counselling for most seats; CUET (ICAR-UG) for about 15 percent of them. -> degree: B.Sc (Hons) Agriculture, 4 years. -> masters: M.Sc in the specialisation. Effectively required for anything beyond field advisory work. -> work: ICAR institute or state agricultural university via the ARS examination, a seed or agri-input company, or an agritech firm.
nuances: [class12_prerequisite] PCB is listed because it is the common requirement, but this is one of the few science professions where Mathematics is accepted in place of Biology at many universities, and where Agriculture is itself a class 12 subject in several state boards. A student should check the specific university rather than assume. || [demand_signal] Moderate, and it splits sharply by employer. ICAR and state agricultural university posts are few and filled by examination; the growth is in private seed, agri-input and agritech companies, which pay better and offer no security. || [entrance_exams] CUET (ICAR-UG) is listed first but is NOT the ordinary way in. It fills only 15 percent of bachelor's seats at the roughly 74 participating agricultural universities; the other 85 percent go through state quotas and state counselling. Treating this national examination as THE gate would overstate how closed agricultural education is by nearly seven times. It is the clearest case in the taxonomy of a famous national exam that most entrants never sit. Source: data/verified_facts.json#icar-aieea-fifteen-percent.

one_liner: Engineers the physical side of farming - machinery, irrigation, storage, processing.
job_roles: Agricultural Engineer | Farm Machinery Engineer | Irrigation Engineer | Post-Harvest & Storage Engineer | Agricultural Structures Engineer | Farm Equipment Service Technician | Micro-Irrigation Designer | Agri-Drone Application Specialist
entrance_exams: JEE Main | CUET (ICAR-UG) | State agricultural university admissions | GATE
self_emp_route: A custom hiring centre - owning machinery and hiring it out with an operator - or a micro-irrigation installation business. Both are the same insight: in Indian agriculture the money is in owning the equipment, not in operating someone else's.
ai_reason: Low exposure. Machinery has to be designed for real field conditions and then repaired in them, and Farm Equipment Service Technician is as safe as any trade in Sector 2. Micro-Irrigation Designer carries some exposure since layout design is increasingly software driven, and Agri-Drone Application Specialist is an occupation that automation CREATED rather than threatens.
role_spread: [Farm Equipment Service Technician] higher: bodily, spatial, conscientiousness / lower: verbal || [Agri-Drone Application Specialist] higher: spatial, logical, confidence / lower: long_term_memory
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics and Mathematics. Chemistry is NOT compulsory for the JEE route; agricultural university counselling may differ and should be checked against the specific university. -> entrance_exam: JEE Main, a state engineering entrance, or agricultural university counselling. -> degree: B.Tech in Agricultural Engineering, offered mainly at agricultural universities rather than at engineering colleges. -> work: Farm machinery manufacturer, an irrigation company, a food processing firm, a state agriculture engineering department, or a custom hiring centre.
nuances: [demand_signal] Moderate and rising for a specific reason: Indian farm labour is becoming scarcer and costlier as rural workers move to construction and services, which is pushing mechanisation on holdings that were previously too small to justify it. Custom hiring is how that reaches a two-hectare farm. || [job_roles] Farm Equipment Service Technician is deliberately inside this profession rather than left out as too junior. It is entered through an ITI, needs no degree, exists in every taluka, and is one of the few technical livelihoods genuinely available to a student who stays in a small town.

one_liner: Turns crops into food that keeps, is safe to eat, and tastes the same every time.
job_roles: Food Technologist | Food Safety & Quality Manager | Product Development Technologist | Food Processing Supervisor | FSSAI Compliance Officer | Sensory Analyst | Dairy Technologist | Packaging Technologist (Food) | Food Microbiologist
entrance_exams: JEE Main | CUET (ICAR-UG) | State agricultural university admissions
self_emp_route: Independent food safety consultancy and FSSAI licensing support for small manufacturers and restaurants, or a small processing unit. The consultancy route is real and growing because compliance obligations now reach very small businesses.
ai_reason: Low exposure, protected by physical product and by regulation. Food has to be made, tested and tasted, and somebody must sign the safety records. Sensory Analyst is the most exposed role on paper - preference modelling from panel data is statistics - but it is protected by needing human panels in the first place. Food Safety & Quality Manager is protected by carrying named responsibility under food law.
role_spread: [Food Safety & Quality Manager, FSSAI Compliance Officer] higher: conscientiousness, attention_span, logical / lower: openness || [Product Development Technologist, Sensory Analyst] higher: openness, naturalistic, reasoning / lower: conscientiousness || [Food Processing Supervisor] higher: bodily, extraversion, conscientiousness / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics, Chemistry and Biology or Mathematics. -> entrance_exam: CUET, a state agricultural university process, or JEE Main for the B.Tech Food Technology route. -> degree: B.Tech or B.Sc in Food Technology, Food Science or Dairy Technology. -> work: A food or dairy processing company, a quality and testing laboratory, a retail or restaurant chain's food safety team, or FSSAI-linked compliance work.
nuances: [class12_prerequisite] Physics and Chemistry only, because listing Biology as well would wrongly shut out PCM students - Food Technology and B.Tech Food Engineering accept Mathematics in place of Biology at most universities. Over-restricting a subject gate is not a safe error in this dataset; it deletes a route a student actually has. || [demand_signal] High, and among the more reliable demand signals in this dataset. It rests on two things that are both still expanding: India's shift from unpackaged to packaged food, and the extension of FSSAI licensing and hygiene obligations down to very small businesses. Both create work that did not exist a decade ago. || [professional_sector] Promised here from Sector 3 rather than kept with the sciences. The method is applied chemistry and microbiology, but the object of concern is food - getting it from a field into a person safely - which is this sector.

one_liner: Keeps animals productive and healthy - milk, poultry, goats, and the systems around them.
job_roles: Dairy Farmer | Dairy Worker | Poultry Farm Supervisor | Livestock Extension Worker | Artificial Insemination Technician | Milk Procurement Officer | Animal Nutrition Specialist | Goat & Small Ruminant Farmer | Para-Veterinary Worker
self_emp_route: Owning animals is the profession for most people in it. A dairy herd of ten crossbred cows supplying a cooperative is a different economic proposition from working on someone else's farm, and it is the standard aspiration.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. Animals are handled, fed, milked and treated by people, in sheds, twice a day, every day. Milk Procurement Officer carries the only real exposure through automated testing and digital payment systems at collection centres, which has already changed that role substantially without removing it.
role_spread: [Artificial Insemination Technician, Para-Veterinary Worker] higher: bodily, conscientiousness, attention_span / lower: extraversion || [Milk Procurement Officer] higher: verbal, extraversion, conscientiousness / lower: bodily || [Poultry Farm Supervisor] higher: logical, attention_span, conscientiousness / lower: openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None for the farm and technician routes; PCB for a B.Sc or B.V.Sc route. -> training: A dairy or livestock diploma, an artificial insemination or para-vet certification, or a Krishi Vigyan Kendra course. Many enter with family experience and no certificate. -> work: Own herd, a dairy cooperative, a private dairy, a commercial poultry or feed company, or the state animal husbandry department. -> scale: Grow the herd, or move into procurement, extension or feed - the routes that convert animal work into a salary.
review_reason: No sourced figure for what a small dairy herd actually earns net of feed, which is the calculation every entrant to this profession is really making, and none for artificial insemination or para-vet technician incomes. The livestock share of household income is sourced; the unit economics of the herd are not.
nuances: [economics] Livestock contributed Rs 1,582 of an agricultural household's Rs 10,218 monthly income in 2018-19 - about 15 percent - and it is the most reliable component because milk sells daily while a crop sells twice a year. That daily cashflow, not the annual total, is why dairy matters to a small farming household. || [demand_signal] High, and India is the world's largest milk producer, but demand here means demand for OUTPUT rather than for salaried posts. Most of this profession is self-employment on a small herd; the salaried roles are in cooperatives, private dairies and feed companies and are far fewer.

one_liner: Grows fruit, vegetables, flowers, tea and spices - the high-value, high-risk end of farming.
job_roles: Horticulturist | Orchard Manager | Floriculture Specialist | Plantation Supervisor | Protected Cultivation & Greenhouse Manager | Nursery Manager | Post-Harvest & Cold Chain Specialist | Landscape & Garden Supervisor | Mushroom & Speciality Crop Grower | Arborist | Tree Pruner
self_emp_route: Growing high-value crops on own or leased land and selling direct - to an exporter, a retail chain, or through a Farmer Producer Organisation. Horticulture is where direct marketing actually changes the economics, because the produce is worth enough to justify the effort.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. Growing, pruning, harvesting and grading are physical work on living plants in a field or a polyhouse. Protected Cultivation & Greenhouse Manager carries a little exposure through automated climate and irrigation control, which is a tool the manager uses rather than a substitute for them.
role_spread: [Plantation Supervisor] higher: extraversion, conscientiousness, bodily / lower: openness || [Protected Cultivation & Greenhouse Manager] higher: logical, attention_span, reasoning / lower: bodily || [Landscape & Garden Supervisor] higher: spatial, openness, extraversion / lower: logical
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream for the practical routes; PCB for a B.Sc Horticulture. -> training: B.Sc Horticulture, a diploma, or a Krishi Vigyan Kendra course. Many growers have none of these. -> work: Own orchard or polyhouse, a plantation company, a nursery, an export packhouse, or a landscaping firm. -> market: Secure a buyer before you plant. In horticulture the market, not the crop, is what fails.
review_reason: No sourced figures for horticulture returns per acre or for plantation sector wages, and the second matters: tea and coffee estate wages are set by state plantation labour rules and are published, which makes them fetchable and would anchor this record the way the NSS survey anchors Farmer.
nuances: [demand_signal] Moderate, and the risk profile is the opposite of staple farming. Horticulture returns several times more per hectare and has no minimum support price, no procurement and very little storage - so a price crash or a delayed truck destroys a season. Higher ceiling, no floor. || [economics] The range understates the upside and hides the variance. A polyhouse of capsicum or a well-marketed orchard can earn many times the figures shown; a season with no buyer earns nothing and the input cost is already spent.

one_liner: Catches or farms fish and shrimp - marine, inland and pond, and the cold chain behind it.
job_roles: Fisherman | Aquaculture Farm Manager | Shrimp Farm Technician | Fisheries Officer | Hatchery Technician | Fish Processing Supervisor | Aquatic Health Specialist | Ornamental Fish Breeder | Fish Seed Producer | Pearl Diver | Shell Gatherer | Chank Diver
entrance_exams: CUET (ICAR-UG) | State agricultural university admissions | State fisheries department recruitment
self_emp_route: Owning ponds, a hatchery or a boat. Aquaculture is one of the higher-return self-employment routes in Indian agriculture and also one of the riskiest - a shrimp crop can fail completely.
ai_reason: Almost unexposed. Fishing, pond management and hatchery work are physical, outdoor and biological. Aquatic Health Specialist and Aquaculture Farm Manager use sensing and water quality monitoring that is increasingly automated, which improves the work rather than replacing the person standing at the pond edge deciding whether to harvest early.
role_spread: [Fisherman] higher: bodily, naturalistic / lower: logical, emotional_stability || [Shrimp Farm Technician, Aquaculture Farm Manager] higher: logical, attention_span, conscientiousness, emotional_stability / lower: - || [Fisheries Officer] higher: verbal, conscientiousness, logical / lower: bodily
path_to_entry: class_11_12: None for capture fishing and farm work; PCB for a B.F.Sc. -> training: B.F.Sc (4 years) for the professional and government routes; on-the-job or a short course for pond and hatchery work. -> work: Own or crew a boat, an aquaculture farm, a hatchery, a processing and export unit, or a state fisheries department. -> scale: Own ponds or a hatchery. In aquaculture the returns and the risk both sit with whoever owns the water.
review_reason: No sourced income figures for Indian capture fishing or for aquaculture returns per hectare, and the two are entirely different economies wrongly sharing one record's numbers. Fishermen's earnings in particular are shaped by boat-owner debt arrangements that no salary range can express.
nuances: [demand_signal] Moderate and export-linked, which is the risk. Indian shrimp aquaculture is built on a small number of export markets and their sanitary and anti-dumping decisions; a single trade action can collapse prices for a season. Inland fish for the domestic market is far steadier and far less profitable. || [job_roles] Fisherman is included as the base layer and should be read with its role_spread entry. Marine capture fishing is among the most dangerous occupations in the country, is largely informal, and is frequently financed by debt to a boat owner - a structure that determines the income more than the catch does.

one_liner: Connects farmers to knowledge, inputs, credit and buyers - the business side of farming.
job_roles: Agricultural Extension Officer | Agri-Input Dealer | Farmer Producer Organisation Manager | Agri-Business Executive | Rural Credit & Agri-Finance Officer | Commodity & Mandi Trader | Agritech Field Executive | Warehouse & Procurement Officer | Krishi Vigyan Kendra Subject Specialist
entrance_exams: State agriculture department recruitment | IBPS PO | CAT | CUET (ICAR-UG) | Agri-business management entrances (IIM Ahmedabad PGP-FABM, IRMA)
self_emp_route: An agri-input dealership, a procurement or trading business, or independent advisory to FPOs and agritech firms. The dealership is the classic route and it is a retail business with a credit book attached.
ai_reason: Moderately exposed, and the exposure lands on the sector's most valuable function. Extension advice - which variety, when to sow, what this leaf spot is - is exactly what farmer advisory apps and image diagnosis now do at zero marginal cost, and Agritech Field Executive and much of Agricultural Extension Officer work is directly substitutable. What survives is where money and trust change hands: Rural Credit & Agri-Finance Officer, Agri-Input Dealer and Farmer Producer Organisation Manager all depend on knowing a specific farmer well enough to lend to them or sell for them.
role_spread: [Rural Credit & Agri-Finance Officer] higher: logical, conscientiousness, reasoning / lower: naturalistic || [Agri-Input Dealer] higher: extraversion, confidence, verbal / lower: openness || [Farmer Producer Organisation Manager] higher: agreeableness, verbal, conscientiousness / lower: confidence
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Any stream for the business roles; PCB or agriculture for extension posts. -> degree: B.Sc Agriculture for extension and technical roles; any degree, or an agri-business MBA, for the commercial ones. -> work: State agriculture department, a Krishi Vigyan Kendra, an input or seed company, a bank's agriculture desk, an agritech firm, or an FPO. -> independence: An input dealership or a procurement and trading business - the two commonest ways people in this profession end up working for themselves.
nuances: [entry_competition] Null. IBPS PO is named in entrance_exams because banks recruit Agriculture Field Officers and it is a genuine well-paid route - but making it the primary_gate would say the way to become an agri-business professional is to pass a banking examination, which is false for almost everyone in this profession. || [demand_signal] High, and it is the part of this sector where salaried jobs actually are. Agriculture employs about 45 percent of Indian workers but almost none of them are employees; the agri-input, agri-finance, agritech and FPO layer is where a graduate finds a salary in this sector. || [job_roles] Agri-Input Dealer is listed with its conflict of interest stated in the role_spread rather than hidden. In most of rural India the person selling the pesticide is also the person advising on whether it is needed, and a student entering this profession should understand that they are entering that position.
